scope: Read-only classification of the retained initial 3,078 passed / 161 failed / 8 ignored workspace transcript; no historical failure is converted to PASS.

provenance.actual_tested_head_or_tree: NOT_RECORDED in the raw transcript; declared base is not proof that the checkout was clean or identical
provenance.github_run_or_job_id: NOT_RECORDED for this historical workspace command
provenance.host_os_and_capabilities: NOT_RECORDED sufficiently to assign all failures to an OS/capability cause

examples.message: called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: ProcessNotVisible { pid: 29486 }

groups.interpretation: The measurement layer returns ProcessNotVisible for 35 fixture process lookups. This establishes unavailable measurement, not its underlying host/process cause.

examples.message: called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: Unavailable { field: "pid_start_time_ticks", reason: "read /proc/30021/stat: No such file or directory (os error 2)" }

groups.interpretation: Execution-binding collection fails because the named /proc/<pid>/stat file cannot be read (ENOENT). These 107 failures occur while constructing live-process inputs, not at their named policy/security assertion. The log alone cannot distinguish absent/inaccessible procfs, namespace visibility or process lifetime.
One self namespace-inode assertion fails. The required namespace link was not established; the log does not identify the host or mount configuration.

examples.message: assertion `left == right` failed: true should have run

groups.interpretation: An allowed real program was expected to exit 0 but instead exited 127; four other enforcement live tests passed. The retained output lacks the enforcement decision/child diagnostics needed to classify this as a source bug versus a host/capability/configuration issue. Keep it an unresolved historical test failure.

examples.message: SoftHSM2 is required for the aip-hsm tests and was not found.

groups.interpretation: Explicit unmet SoftHSM2/PKCS#11 dependency. All 15 fail in the shared module-discovery setup before custody assertions run. The tests intentionally refuse to skip this dependency.

examples.message: assertion `left == right` failed: a rejected program is EACCES, not Operation not permitted (os error 1)

groups.interpretation: Map creation succeeded, but unsafe-program loading returned EPERM (1) while the test expected verifier EACCES (13). The test only guards map creation before requiring a verifier rejection, so program-load availability is not separately established. EPERM does not prove that the kernel verifier evaluated and rejected the unsafe access; this is a concrete test/harness availability distinction, not evidence of an accepted unsafe program.

examples.message: this process is alive and started before now

groups.interpretation: One socket-sending-task start-tick anchor returns no value. The message alone does not distinguish unavailable /proc inputs from clock/instance timing.

conclusions: 142 failures explicitly report unavailable /proc stat/process measurement; the namespace-inode failure and socket-task-anchor failure are tracked separately rather than assumed to share an identical cause.
15 explicitly require the missing SoftHSM module. The two remaining exceptions are enforcement exit127 and XDP program-load EPERM, retained individually with unresolved/limited causes.
The initial run remains failed. These categories describe observed failure mechanisms and do not prove every underlying root cause was environmental.

No new source fixes are made from this historical classification. Current supported Linux results must be linked separately at their exact source; optional capability-return paths do not by themselves prove kernel functionality.
